claims.text: Machine-learning-driven optimization of dealloying conditions can enable synthesis of three-dimensional noble-metal-based high-entropy-alloy nanoframeworks.
Machine-learning-guided dealloying can enhance atomic control in NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
Machine-learning-guided dealloying can enhance the catalytic performance of NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
A data-driven machine-learning framework can predict optimal chemical or electrochemical dealloying parameters.
Etchant concentration, temperature, and dealloying duration can be precisely regulated according to machine-learning predictions.
The proposed treatment forms well-defined three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The resulting nanoframeworks have a uniform elemental distribution.
The resulting nanoframeworks have a controlled surface structure.
The machine-learning framework leverages large datasets from prior experiments and simulations.
Machine-learning-selected dealloying conditions promote controlled atomic-scale phase separation.
Machine-learning-selected dealloying conditions promote controlled removal of less-noble elements.
Controlled phase separation and removal of less-noble elements yield three-dimensional structures with precise atomic arrangements.
Machine-learning-guided dealloying produces greater atomic control than conventional dealloying.
Improved atomic control leads to greater catalytic activity than is obtained with conventional dealloying.
Expected improvements depend on the availability of high-quality machine-learning training data.
Expected improvements depend on the ability to precisely control dealloying parameters.
